questions.title: Palindrome After Cleaning
questions.description:
Read a single line of text — it may contain spaces, punctuation and digits — and decide whether it is a **palindrome once you ignore everything except letters and digits**.

### Cleaning rules

1. Remove every character that is **not** a letter (`a`-`z`, `A`-`Z`) or a digit (`0`-`9`) — this drops spaces, commas, periods, colons, apostrophes, question marks, etc.
2. Lower-case whatever letters remain.

Then check whether the cleaned string reads the same forwards and backwards.

If the line has **no** letters or digits at all (for example it is empty, all spaces, or only punctuation), the cleaned string is the empty string — and the empty string counts as a palindrome, so the answer is `YES`.

### Input

A single line (it may be empty).

### Output

Print exactly `YES` if the cleaned string is a palindrome, otherwise print exactly `NO`.

### Example

Input:
```
A man, a plan, a canal: Panama
```

Cleaning keeps only letters/digits and lower-cases them: `amanaplanacanalpanama`, which reads the same backwards. Output:
```
YES
```

testCases.description: classic sentence palindrome with punctuation and spaces
testCases.input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

testCases.description: single character is trivially a palindrome
only punctuation and spaces -> empty after cleaning -> YES
